title: add lightweight cpu-gpu-sync-latency-probe-and-waterfall-export
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Adds low-overhead CPU/GPU sync latency probe, a waterfall timeline exporter consumable by perf dashboards, and a small microbench harness for synthetic kernel scheduling scenarios. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: We see intermittent end-to-end spikes where CPU scheduling waits for GPU-side work (kernel enqueue vs. completion) and our existing NVTX ranges + counters were insufficient to correlate fine-grained CPU->GPU handoffs. This PR introduces a low-overhead 'cpu_gpu_sync' probe that timestamps enqueue, launch_ack, and completion acknowledgment points (with a path for optional NVTX annotation), plus a compact waterfall JSON exporter that groups per-request CPU and GPU segments for visualizing interleaving across worker threads and CUDA streams.

What this change does: - Adds runtime/instr/cpu_gpu_sync.{h,cc} implementing a tiny ring buffer sampler (lock-free, pre-allocated) keyed by request id and epoch. The probe is enabled via runtime flags and is optimized for hot paths (fast-path inlined timestamp + tag write). - Adds scheduler hooks (runtime/scheduler/sync_hooks.cc) to record enqueue->dispatch->completion edges. Hooks are fenced to avoid instrumentation during shutdown. - Adds exporter: tools/perf/exporters/waterfall_exporter.cc which reads the ring buffer and emits a compact per-request waterfall JSON (versions v1/v2) suitable for ingestion by our perf dashboard and ad-hoc analysis (speedscope + chrome-trace compatible fragments). - Adds microbench: infra/microbench/cpu_gpu_sync_bench.{cc,py} with small scenarios (single-threaded burst, multi-threaded small batches, and KV-cache primed paths) that exercise enqueue latency and observe tail behavior. - Adds lightweight counters: runtime/instr/counters.h with per-thread occupancy counters and a cumulative sync-wait histogram (HDR-like buckets, but stored as flat counts to avoid dynamic allocations). - Adds docs: docs/perf/instrumentation/cpu_gpu_sync.md with enabling flags and examples of waterfall output.

Checklist: [x] unit tests for ring buffer safety (sanity) [x] microbench harness and CI smoke [x] perf exporter small integration test [x] docs and runbook entry for how to use waterfall traces for RCA

Small illustrative snippet (in description form): ``// fast path: record enqueue timestamp
inline void record_enqueue(uint64_t req_id) { if (!enabled) return; auto t = clock::now_ns(); rb_.write(req_id, TAG_ENQUEUE, t); }``

Testing and results: - CI: bench-smoke pipeline runs the microbench scenarios; results embedded as artifacts (waterfall JSON + simple CSV summary). - Local perf runs (NVIDIA A100, sequence_len=1024 synthetic) show the exporter can capture sub-200us host->device handoff variance on steady-state but reveals outlier clusters when scheduler batching increases queue depth. - Overhead measured: typical per-request instrumentation adds ~120ns on the hot path when NVTX is disabled, ~450ns when NVTX annotation path is taken. We added a runtime knob to turn NVTX tagging on only for debug captures.

Backward compatibility and safety: The ring buffer defaults to 0 (disabled) in prod; enabling requires an env flag or console toggle. The implementation avoids allocations on hot path and uses per-thread pre-allocated buffers to bound tail latency. Exporter reads buffers with a simple epoch gating to avoid partial records.

Follow-ups: - Add a dashboard ingest pipeline to aggregate waterfall traces by request template (ENG-9310) - Add a condensed per-route tail report that summarizes sync-wait percentiles - Consider an optional lightweight on-host correlator that tags traces with syscall-level latencies for deeper RCA

Notes for reviewers: focus on correctness of ring buffer memory model (lock-free semantics), scheduler hook placement (no preemption/instrumentation during critical sections), and the waterfall schema (v1 chosen to be compact).
